# Policy-KB bijection audit — catering_order_desk / task 1

Scope: product **catering**, 53 published documents; the difficulty's `catering.extended.yaml`,
`task_tools.py`, and `tasks/1.json`. Entry conditions cited from the brief: policy-side verdict
PASSED at round 3; `check_docs.py` on `catering` returned `DOCS OK`; `check_traceability.py` on
`tasks/catering_order_desk` returned `TRACEABILITY OK`. The auditor ran neither and is independent
of the render agent and of the policy-side auditor.

The blind answer for this task was frozen to
`audits/runtime_context/catering_order_desk/1.md` before any source-layer material was opened.

## kb_to_source

**C1 — `programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326`: the tier condition is carried
faithfully, and the figure it turns on is not resolvable inside this product. Reported here as the
source of the task's `KB-RUNTIME RED`; not counted as a bijection failure of the catering corpus.**

The document states, twice and in a table:

> "Where the client holds a private event and banquet agreement billing under the same client
> account code as the Corporate Catering Service Agreement, that agreement stands open and its
> package **is written for 200 guests or more**, a programme concession of 4 percentage points …
> is taken on the value standing."

and

> "Against that account code the client's Private Event & Banquet Services agreement is read for two
> things: whether it stands open, and how many guests the package recorded on it is written for."

*Faithful to the source.* The source ladder reads "its package is written for two hundred guests or
more" and "whose package is written for fewer than two hundred guests". The render carries both,
with the figures, the matching key and the records named, and it names the other product by its
official name. On the render side nothing was dropped, softened or added.

*Where it fails.* The figure the condition turns on is stated nowhere in the catering corpus, and
`find_banquet_agreements` returns no guest count — only `variant_name 'Seated Banquet Package'`. The
reader must therefore go to the Private Event & Banquet Services corpus, where
`docs/banquet/package_capacity_and_lead_schedule_1a8137ad.json` prints the two columns (60 and 350
for that package) and defines them:

> "The smallest guest count is the guest count the package **is written for** and the largest is the
> guest count the package **handles**."

That definitional sentence sends "written for" to 60 — fewer than 200 — and so to the 2.0-point
tier. The source binds the same words to the other column:
`compute[16] banquet_max_guests: CPARAM('banquet','max_guests', client_account_code=…)`, where the
banquet parameter schema describes `max_guests` as "largest guest count the package handles" and
`min_guests` as "smallest guest count the package is written for". The GT trace says so in terms:
"a Seated Banquet Package … which stands active and **is written for 350 guests**, two hundred or
more".

*Consequence on this task.* The visible corpus yields a programme concession of 2.0 points, a total
concession rate of 8.5, a value standing of 5215.50 and a cancellation charge of 1440.78; the source
layer expects 4.0, 10.5, 5101.50 and 1409.29. Both scored parameters of this task are affected.

*Nature of the defect.* It originates on the policy side — the ladder's condition is worded in the
vocabulary of one parameter and bound to another — and the catering documents carry that wording
verbatim, as the render skill requires them to. It is therefore recorded as `KB-RUNTIME RED` on this
task (the visible materials do not entail the source's solution) and as a policy-side note on its
origin, and it is **not** recorded as `KB-BIJECTION RED`: the ladder is carried in full, every tier
exact, with the product named and the records named.

**C2 — `cancellation_notice_and_charges_2873d9a3`, the live three-way notice sentence. Policy-side
note.**

> "Notice at or beyond the free-cancellation hours printed against the service level carries no
> charge at all; notice inside that window but before the service day carries the within-notice
> percentage of the order value; and notice on the service day itself carries the same-day
> percentage of the order value."

This sentence belongs to the base rule `catering_cancellation_charges` and is not retired by any
`overwrite`, so the KB carries it as the source has it — base law the KB may neither drop nor
soften. It orders the bands free-window-first, while the live factor
`percentage_the_notice_given_yields_b980fca9` orders them service-day-first and says so in terms.
The two disagree only where notice is given on the service day *and* the counted notice reaches the
free-cancellation hours, which the notice-counting factor makes reachable (the account-manager tier
adds a day). Neither task in this difficulty lands there — task 1's notice is given two days out on
a level whose free window is 72 hours. Recorded as a policy-side note under Step 4, not as a KB
verdict.

**C3 — findings B1, B2 and B3 recorded in `policy_kb/catering_order_desk/0.md`** (the cafe-kitchen
concession parameter rendered under the live concession's name; the two volume ladders; the
intermediate-rounding wording) are corpus-wide and stand for this task too. None of the three bears
on task 1's world: its client holds no cafe contract, and the invoicing policy is outside its
charter scope.

**No additions found.** The pattern scans described in `policy_kb/catering_order_desk/0.md` —
cross-problem operational guidance, procedure/checklist/route language, unsourced confirmation,
review, notification or escalation obligations, and seeded world state written in as policy fact
(caller names, `CA-22853`, `CS-271`, `CO-7xxxxx`, 17812.5, 6400, 5700, literal 2025-/2026- dates) —
returned nothing across all 53 documents.

## revision_2

Round 2, 2026-09-22. Revision 1's sections above are left untouched.

Entry conditions cited from the coordinator and not re-run by me: `check_docs.py` on `catering`
returned `DOCS OK` with the same shape as round 1; `check_traceability.py` on
`tasks/catering_order_desk` returned `TRACEABILITY OK`. Six of 53 documents changed; none added,
removed or renamed, confirmed by diffing the corpus dump against my revision-1 copy.

### Round-1 item C1 — closed

Revision 1 recorded that `programme_concession_from_a_banquet_agreement_5e738326` selected its tier
on what a banquet package "is written for", a phrase the banquet schedule defines as the package's
*smallest* guest count, while the source bound the condition to `max_guests`; and that the catering
document carried the source's ladder word for word, so the drift was in the source.

**The source was corrected.** Diffing the charter against my revision-1 dump, the ladder of
`programme_concession_taken` now reads:

> tier 0 — "the client holds a private event and banquet agreement billing under the same client
> account code as the catering agreement, that agreement **stands active** and **the largest guest
> count its package handles** reaches two hundred"
> tier 1 — "… that **stands active** and **the largest guest count its package handles falls short
> of** two hundred"

and the `compute` block is **byte-identical** to revision 1 — `banquet_max_guests` is still
`CPARAM('banquet','max_guests', client_account_code=F('client_account_code'))`. The wording was
moved onto the binding it always read, which is the right direction of repair: the alternative,
moving the binding to `min_guests`, would have changed what the policy computes.

**The KB carries the correction exactly.** Every tier, the "Otherwise" tier, the matching key, the
records-read paragraph, the four-row table and the boundary sentence all now use "stands active" and
"the largest guest count its package handles". The boundary is still adjudicated in figures — "A
package whose largest guest count handled is exactly 200 reaches 200 and carries the concession of
4.0 per cent; one whose largest guest count handled is 199 falls short of 200 and carries 2.0 per
cent" — and the account-code exclusion is still stated. Nothing was dropped in the rewrite.

**It now resolves uniquely, and I tested that rather than assuming it.** The rival readings and
their status are enumerated in `runtime_context/catering_order_desk/1.md` revision_2; in summary,
"largest guest count … handles" names one column, the banquet schedule gives that column its own
verb ("the largest is the guest count the package handles") and gives the other column a different
one ("is written for"), "Largest guest count" appears in exactly one banquet document, and "stands
active" matches the record's `status` value literally against a four-state lifecycle. Re-derived
from the published documents, the pair is 5101.50 and 1409.29, which is the source layer's.

**C1: CLOSED.**

### The unprompted fix, judged

`order_value_and_guest_count_schedule_abd24923` is the document revision 1 named as the corpus's
only support for the misreading — it wrote "the smallest and largest guest counts it **is written
for**", lending the loose band-sense of the phrase. It now reads "the smallest guest count it **is
written for**, the largest guest count it **handles**", and its Points-of-judgement sentence changed
"is written for a small room" to "serves a small room".

Checked against the source: the catering `parameter_schema` describes `min_headcount` as "smallest
guest count the service level is written for" and `max_headcount` as "largest guest count the
service level handles without a separate event agreement" — the same convention the banquet schema
uses. The document now matches its own schema. All figures in the table are unchanged (confirmed by
the per-variant cell sweep). This was worth doing: it removes the last place in the catering corpus
where "written for" could be read as covering a band, and it was not asked for.

A corpus-wide sweep leaves five occurrences of "written for", **none of them a guest-count sense** —
four are the drafting sense ("both rows are written for a contract standing active", "the second
branch is written for a record of at least 3 and fewer than 6", "no band is written for a single
invoiced order", "the first two rows are written for a contract that stands active") and the fifth
is the corrected schedule sentence above.

### The withdrawn framing phrase

`percentage_the_notice_given_yields_b980fca9` no longer says the bands are "tested in the order set
out here". Revision 1 cited that phrase approvingly, so I checked what its removal costs. The
document still states, as a rule rather than as an instruction for reading it: "notice given on the
service day is on that band whatever the hours would otherwise have come to." That is precisely the
precedence the source's `compute` fixes (`cancellation_fee_pct_same_day if notice_days <= 0 else …`),
and it is the *only* precedence the ladder needs, because band 3 is "otherwise" and so cannot
overlap band 2. Nothing was lost and a reading instruction was removed. A corpus sweep confirms zero
remaining occurrences of the phrase.

Leaving the analogous sentence in `volume_step_on_catering_spend_4b595156` ("A band is tested from
the top of the table down, and the first band whose spend figure and whose order count are both met
is the band the agreement earns") is the right call and not an inconsistency: the three volume bands
genuinely overlap on spend — 40000.00 also reaches 15000.00 and 5000.00 — no other sentence orders
them, and the source's nested tiers entail the top-down test. There the sentence is load-bearing;
in the notice-band document it was not.

### The three declines

Judged on their merits in `policy_kb/catering_order_desk/0.md` revision_2. In short: I **accept all
three** — intermediate rounding, notice-band ordering and the two volume ladders — on the ground the
renderer gives, that the render may not close what the source leaves open nor publish a precision
the source's own rule text does not state. None is re-raised against the render layer. All three are
re-raised as standing **policy-side notes** for the source layer: the charter's `rule` text and its
`compute` disagree about where rounding falls; an un-retired base sentence orders the notice bands
differently from the live factor (reachable only on a Drop-Off account with same-day account-manager
notice, which neither task reaches); and a per-variant parameter whose only operative clause is
retired is still carried as live — the same shape as B1, which is exactly why B1's fix had to keep
the atom rather than delete it.
